implementation_notes: TypeORM hands the pattern over: dataSource.getRepository(Order) returns a Repository<Order> with find({ where }), findOneBy, save and remove, typed by the entity class, and EntityManager.transaction or a QueryRunner is the unit of work. A hand-written class is unnecessary unless the domain must not import TypeORM, in which case define the interface in the domain and implement it in infrastructure, mapping entities to domain types at the boundary.
pitfalls: Decorated entity classes are not domain objects: reusing them keeps persistence metadata in the domain and makes the model hard to construct in tests; map at the boundary when that matters.
Lazy relations return promises resolved through an active manager, so accessing them after the request scope closes throws instead of loading.
Eager relations multiply joined rows silently; enable query logging on read paths and check what the collection call actually executes.

variants.name: Prisma generated client (typed query API, no repository class)
variants.implementation_notes: Prisma generates a typed client from the schema: prisma.order.findMany({ where: { due: { lt: on } } }) is the collection-like surface, $transaction is the unit of work, and results are plain objects - there is no entity class and no repository object to write. Wrap the client in a module or class when a domain-language interface or a substitution point is needed; otherwise the client itself is the repository surface, which means the ORM choice leaks into the domain unless it is wrapped.
pitfalls: Prisma returns plain data rather than tracked entities, so read-modify-write needs an explicit update inside $transaction plus optimistic locking, or lost updates are the default.
include and nested writes can hide N+1 reads or unintended cascades; enable query logging for critical paths.

Generated types are tied to the schema: renaming a field becomes a compile error across the domain if the clients types are used directly, so wrap the client when the domain must not follow the schema.
